resolutions.researcher_notes: The live BusinessWire URL 403s to automated fetchers (confirmed via curl, not a deletion); its Wayback capture (2024-06-12) is live and reads: 'the Trans-Pecos Pipeline and the Comanche Trail Pipeline...are in service...The Comanche Trail Pipeline...went into service as scheduled on January 30, 2017' (Energy Transfer press release, May 3, 2017). Independently, EIA's public 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' historical dataset (govt source, downloaded and read directly with openpyxl) lists Comanche Trail Pipeline, Status='Completed', Completed Date=2017-01-30, Year In Service=2017. Two distinct publishers (Energy Transfer/BusinessWire and EIA) agree the line entered service and completed construction in Jan 2017, i.e. operating. No news of any subsequent shutdown found.

Both sources describe Comanche Trail explicitly as a natural gas pipeline transporting gas from the Waha Hub; EIA's dataset lists it under 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects'. Two distinct publishers agree.

'Transmission' is inferred, not literal, in both sources. BusinessWire describes a 195-mile, 42-inch, FERC/DOE-authorized long-haul pipeline moving gas from the Waha production hub to a Mexico export point with seven delivery taps; EIA's dataset classifies it a 'New Pipeline' regulated by FERC under Docket CP15-503 as 'Interstate'. That combination (large-diameter, long-distance, FERC-jurisdictional, hub-to-border haul) is the standard profile GEM classifies as transmission rather than gathering/distribution, but since neither source uses the word 'transmission' itself I am marking this medium/non-independent rather than claiming a literal two-source match.

BusinessWire: 'The Comanche Trail Pipeline and the WAHA Header went into service as scheduled on January 30, 2017.' EIA dataset: Completed Date 2017-01-30, Year In Service 2017. Exact date agreement between Energy Transfer (via BusinessWire) and EIA, two distinct publishers -> StartYear1=2017 confirmed.
BusinessWire: 'designed to transport 1.1 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas' = 1,100 MMcf/d. EIA dataset: Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) = 1100. Exact numeric agreement, two distinct publishers.

BusinessWire: 'The 42-inch intrastate pipeline traverses 195 miles through Pecos, Reeves, Culberson, Hudspeth, and El Paso counties.' EIA dataset: Miles = 195. Exact numeric agreement, two distinct publishers.

BusinessWire: '42-inch intrastate pipeline'. EIA dataset: Pipeline Diameter (Inches) = 42. BNamericas (fetched live, 200): 'a 42-inch natural gas pipeline from the Waha Hub to the Mexico-US border near San Elizario, Texas.' Three distinct publishers, exact agreement.

BusinessWire: pipeline moves 'natural gas from the Waha Hub in Pecos County, Texas'. BNamericas: 'a 42-inch natural gas pipeline from the Waha Hub'. Both name the Waha Hub/Waha Field as the supply source, two distinct publishers.

BusinessWire: pipeline 'terminates...at the Texas-Mexico border in San Elizario, Texas, just south of El Paso, Texas', traversing Pecos, Reeves, Culberson, Hudspeth and El Paso counties, Texas (start end). BNamericas: 'from the Waha Hub to the Mexico-US border near San Elizario, Texas.' Both confirm StartState=Texas and EndPrefecture/District=San Elizario, Texas, two distinct publishers.

EIA's public 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' historical dataset lists Comanche Trail Pipeline, Cost (millions) = 2.5, i.e. $2,500,000 -- exact match to the sheet's SegmentCost. Single source only (I could not find a second independent statement of this cost; the other seed citations that might address cost -- IJGlobal's project pages -- are paywalled search/login surfaces I could not verify content on, so I did not cite them). CONCERN (informational, not proposing a value change): $2.5M looks low for a cross-border 195-mile/42-inch pipeline built as part of a CFE tender (peer pipelines of similar scope have run into the hundreds of millions); it is possible this figure is a partial/allocated cost rather than total project capex, or an error EIA inherited from the same original filing GEM's number traces to. Flagging for awareness only -- not changing the value.

MasTec, Inc.'s SEC Form 10-K (FY2015, filed 2016-02-26), Exhibit 21 subsidiaries list: 'Comanche Trail Pipeline, LLC (33% owned by MasTec Comanche, LLC) (16% owned by Energy Transfer Mexicana, LLC) (51% owned by Carso Energy Corp.)' -- exact match to the sheet's Owner1=Carso Energy 51%, Owner2=MasTec 33%, Owner3=Energy Transfer 16%. BNamericas independently names the same three parties (Energy Transfer Partners, Mastec Inc., Carso Energy) as the winning CFE-tender consortium (without percentages). Two distinct entities (MasTec's own SEC filing and BNamericas' independent project profile) agree on the ownership group; percentages come from the SEC filing specifically.
